explanation: x86-64 assembly language is the low-level language directly executed by the processor. Understanding its control flow instructions, like jumps and conditional jumps, is crucial for optimizing performance and interacting directly with hardware.  Control flow alters the sequential execution of instructions, enabling complex program behavior and efficient algorithm implementation.

extraction_metadata.source: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)

book: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)
code_example:
mov     rcx, 10     ; Loop counter
_loop:
    cmp     rcx, 0      ; Compare RCX to zero
    je      _done       ; Jump if Equal (ZF=1)

    cmp     rax, rbx    ; Compare data values
    jg      _swap       ; Jump if Greater (Signed)
    jl      _skip       ; Jump if Less (Signed)

_swap:
    call    _utility    ; Procedure Call (Pushes RIP)

_skip:
    dec     rcx
    jmp     _loop       ; Unconditional jump

_done:
    ret                 ; Return (Pops RIP)
keywords: x64 assembly, assembly jump instructions, x86 control flow
